label: Ski
blurb: Resorts and backcountry areas with the runs people cross oceans for.

places.name: Vail
places.why: The largest single-mountain resort in the US, a sprawl of groomed Back Bowls that draws skiers from across the world.

places.name: Beaver Creek
places.why: A manicured, ski-in-ski-out sister to Vail known for grooming so precise locals call it corduroy heaven.

places.name: Aspen Mountain
places.why: Steep, lift-served terrain rising straight out of a historic mining town with no beginner runs to dilute it.

places.name: Aspen Highlands
places.why: Highland Bowl's 40-minute bootpack rewards skiers with some of the steepest inbounds pitches in North America.

places.name: Snowmass
places.why: The biggest of Aspen's four mountains, built for long cruisers and a family base village.

places.name: Breckenridge
places.why: Five peaks over 12,000 feet and an old mining-town base give it the biggest lift-served vertical in Colorado.

places.name: Keystone
places.why: Colorado's biggest night-skiing operation, with A-Basin-adjacent terrain and reliable family grooming.

places.name: Copper Mountain
places.why: Naturally divided terrain puts beginners, cruisers and experts on separate parts of the mountain by design.

places.name: Winter Park
places.why: Mary Jane's mogul fields are a rite of passage, right off Denver's Amtrak Winter Park Express.

places.name: Steamboat
places.why: Champagne Powder country, with gladed aspen groves that made tree skiing a Colorado signature.

places.name: Telluride
places.why: A free gondola links a perfectly preserved Victorian mining town to some of Colorado's gnarliest extreme terrain.

places.name: Crested Butte
places.why: Extreme Limits terrain off the North Face put this old coal town on the map for steep, technical skiing.

places.name: Silverton Mountain
places.why: One double chair, mandatory guiding and avalanche gear, and nothing but big, steep, ungroomed terrain.

places.name: Wolf Creek
places.why: No real-estate development at all, just Colorado's snowiest resort catching every storm off the San Juans.

places.name: Arapahoe Basin
places.why: One of the highest lift-served ski areas in the US, often spinning lifts into June off its East Wall.

places.name: Monarch Mountain
places.why: A small, unglitzy Continental Divide resort that quietly racks up some of Colorado's most consistent snowfall.

places.name: Park City Mountain
places.why: North America's largest single ski resort by acreage, joined to Canyons under one lift ticket.

places.name: Deer Valley
places.why: Skiers-only grooming and a famously polished guest-service standard, plus real Utah powder days.

places.name: Alta
places.why: Skiers-only since 1938, with some of the lightest, driest lake-effect powder anywhere on earth.

places.name: Snowbird
places.why: A tram climbing 2,900 vertical feet into some of the steepest, snowiest inbounds terrain in the Wasatch.

places.name: Snowbasin
places.why: 2002 Olympic downhill terrain with a base lodge finish more like a national park than a ski hill.

places.name: Powder Mountain
places.why: More skiable acres than lifts to reach them, so a huge share of the mountain stays untracked for days.

places.name: Jackson Hole
places.why: Corbet's Couloir and 4,139 feet of continuous vertical made this the American benchmark for expert terrain.

places.name: Grand Targhee
places.why: On the quiet side of the Tetons, catching over 500 inches of some of the lightest snow in the Rockies.

places.name: Big Sky
places.why: Lone Peak's tram opens genuine no-fall-zone couloirs above a resort with room for 5,800 skiers max.

places.name: Whitefish Mountain Resort
places.why: Snow ghosts of rime-caked trees and views to Glacier National Park on a lightly crowded northern Rockies hill.

places.name: Bridger Bowl
places.why: A skier-owned nonprofit hill famous for the Ridge, a hike-to ridgeline of steep chutes above the lifts.

places.name: Sun Valley
places.why: America's first destination ski resort, opened in 1936, still grooming Bald Mountain to a glassy finish.

places.name: Schweitzer
places.why: Panhandle powder over views of Lake Pend Oreille, with far fewer crowds than its size deserves.

places.name: Palisades Tahoe
places.why: Host of the 1960 Winter Olympics, with KT-22 among the most demanding lift-served faces in the Sierra.

places.name: Mammoth Mountain
places.why: A volcanic dome catching Sierra cement in bulk, with a season that regularly runs into June.

places.name: Heavenly
places.why: Gondola views straight down onto Lake Tahoe from runs that straddle the California-Nevada line.

places.name: Kirkwood
places.why: The snowiest resort in the Tahoe basin, with cliff-lined bowls that keep it a magnet for expert skiers.

places.name: Mount Bachelor
places.why: A near-symmetrical volcanic cone with 360-degree lift-served terrain and a long, snowy spring season.

places.name: Crystal Mountain
places.why: Washington's biggest resort, with Mount Rainier filling the skyline from its high alpine bowls.

places.name: Mount Baker
places.why: Holder of the world record snowfall for a single season, with a laid-back, no-frills powder culture.

places.name: Taos Ski Valley
places.why: A ski school founded on European technique and steep, high-altitude terrain above a small adobe base.

places.name: Stowe
places.why: Vermont's highest peak, Mount Mansfield, delivers New England's most genuinely steep lift-served skiing.

places.name: Killington
places.why: The Beast of the East runs 200-plus trails and often the longest season in the eastern US thanks to snowmaking.

places.name: Sugarbush
places.why: Twin peaks of old-school Vermont steep and deep, with Castlerock left ungroomed on purpose.

places.name: Mad River Glen
places.why: Skier-owned and single-chair served, with a ridgeline so ungroomed the motto is simply Ski It If You Can.

places.name: Sugarloaf
places.why: The only lift-served above-treeline skiing in the eastern US, exposed on Maine's second-highest peak.

places.name: Whiteface Mountain
places.why: Site of the 1980 Lake Placid Olympic downhill, with the biggest vertical drop in the eastern US.

places.name: Alyeska Resort
places.why: Coastal Chugach snowfall dumped straight off the Gulf of Alaska onto lift-served, avalanche-controlled terrain.

places.name: Valdez / Thompson Pass
places.why: The birthplace of big-mountain heli skiing, where Chugach spines rise straight out of the sea in near-constant snow.

places.name: Haines
places.why: Steep, glaciated Chilkat and Takshanuk terrain that made Southeast Alaska a heli-skiing pilgrimage.

places.name: Whistler Blackcomb
places.why: North America's biggest ski area by vertical, joined by the Peak 2 Peak gondola between two glaciated giants.

places.name: Revelstoke Mountain Resort
places.why: North America's greatest continuous vertical drop, in the heart of the Selkirks' legendary snowfall.

places.name: Lake Louise
places.why: Four mountain faces above a turquoise glacial lake, inside one of the most scenic ski areas on the continent.

places.name: Sunshine Village
places.why: Straddling the Continental Divide with the most reliable natural snow in the Canadian Rockies.

places.name: Mount Norquay
places.why: A steep, old-school Banff local's hill with the North American chairlift-served terrain that stays uncrowded.

places.name: Kicking Horse
places.why: One of the highest vertical drops in Canada, with alpine bowls above treeline reached straight from a gondola.

places.name: Fernie Alpine Resort
places.why: Five alpine bowls in the Lizard Range catch huge Kootenay snowfall right off the lifts.

places.name: Red Mountain Resort
places.why: A gritty, uncrowded Kootenay classic with some of the best lift-served tree skiing anywhere.

places.name: Panorama Mountain Resort
places.why: Purcell Mountain views over a big vertical drop, plus cat-skiing access to terrain beyond the boundary.

places.name: Big White
places.why: Famous for its rime-frosted snow ghosts and deep, dry Okanagan powder on family-friendly slopes.

places.name: SilverStar Mountain Resort
places.why: A brightly painted Victorian-style village base with dry Okanagan powder and long groomers above.

places.name: Sun Peaks Resort
places.why: Canada's second-largest ski area, spread over three mountains with a walkable Alpine-style village.

places.name: Whitewater Ski Resort
places.why: A small, snow-obsessed Kootenay hill with steep, ungroomed terrain and legendary powder days.

places.name: Apex Mountain Resort
places.why: A small, low-key Okanagan resort valued for uncrowded groomers and a tight, walkable base village.

places.name: Kimberley Alpine Resort
places.why: A Bavarian-themed East Kootenay town resort with reliable snow and none of the coastal crowds.

places.name: Castle Mountain Resort
places.why: A remote, uncrowded southern Alberta resort known among locals for its steep, wide-open alpine bowls.

places.name: Marmot Basin
places.why: Wide, uncrowded alpine bowls inside Jasper National Park, with some of the driest snow in the Rockies.

places.name: Mont Tremblant
places.why: The Laurentians' biggest vertical and a lively pedestrian village built around a historic mountain.

places.name: Le Massif de Charlevoix
places.why: The highest vertical drop east of the Rockies, with runs that finish almost on the St. Lawrence shore.

places.name: Mont-Sainte-Anne
places.why: One of eastern Canada's biggest ski areas, close enough to Quebec City for an easy day trip.

places.name: CMH Bugaboo Lodge
places.why: Where mechanized heli-skiing began in 1965, dropping skiers onto glaciated Purcell peaks all week from a fly-in lodge.

places.name: CMH Monashees
places.why: Deep, consistent Monashee snowfall and low-angle glades that made this one of CMH's most sought-after heli zones.

places.name: Selkirk Wilderness Skiing
places.why: One of the original cat-skiing operations, working legendary Selkirk snowfall from a single remote lodge.

places.name: Island Lake Catskiing
places.why: Cat-skiing through old-growth glades and alpine bowls on private tenure beside Fernie's resort boundary.

places.name: Baldface Lodge
places.why: A remote, off-grid cat-ski lodge in the Selkirks known for steep tree runs and huge total snowfall.

places.name: Whistler Heli-Skiing (Coast Mountains)
places.why: Coast Mountains heli access to glaciers and alpine bowls well beyond Whistler Blackcomb's lift network.

places.name: Chamonix
places.why: Base town for the Vallée Blanche and the Aiguille du Midi téléphérique, the birthplace of extreme skiing.

places.name: Vallée Blanche
places.why: A 20 km off-piste glacier descent from the Aiguille du Midi, the most famous ungroomed run in the world.

places.name: Les Grands Montets
places.why: Steep, high-alpine terrain above Argentière that has drawn extreme skiers since the 1970s.

places.name: Val d'Isère
places.why: Half of the vast Espace Killy, with a race pedigree and some of the best off-piste terrain in the Alps.

places.name: Tignes
places.why: Glacier skiing on the Grande Motte keeps runs open into autumn above Val d'Isère's shared valley.

places.name: Courchevel
places.why: The most polished of the Trois Vallées bases, with a valley-served altiport and Michelin-heavy après.

places.name: Méribel
places.why: The central hub of the Trois Vallées, the largest linked ski area on earth.

places.name: Val Thorens
places.why: Europe's highest ski resort, with snow-sure glacier access at the top of the Trois Vallées.

places.name: Les Deux Alpes
places.why: Year-round glacier skiing on the Dôme, plus a big French ski-town party scene at the base.

places.name: Alpe d'Huez
places.why: The Sarenne, at 16 km one of the longest black runs in the world, drops off this sun-drenched resort.

places.name: La Grave
places.why: A single téléphérique with no marked pistes at all, serving some of the most serious off-piste terrain in Europe.

places.name: Serre Chevalier
places.why: A long, sunny valley of linked villages with a huge, varied terrain network in the southern French Alps.

places.name: Les Arcs
places.why: Part of the Paradiski network, with wide-open alpine bowls built for high-speed cruising.

places.name: La Plagne
places.why: Ten linked villages and the 1992 Olympic bobsled track, joined to Les Arcs by the Vanoise Express.

places.name: Avoriaz / Portes du Soleil
places.why: A car-free, timber-clad resort anchoring the cross-border Portes du Soleil, the world's largest linked lift network.

places.name: Megève
places.why: An elegant, low-key Haute-Savoie village resort favoured for gentle terrain and old-money charm.

places.name: Saint-Lary-Soulan
places.why: The biggest ski area in the French Pyrenees, with a cable car climbing straight from the village.

places.name: Zermatt
places.why: Skiing under the Matterhorn on a car-free glacier resort linked year-round across the border to Cervinia.

places.name: Verbier
places.why: The steep, off-piste heart of the Four Valleys, and one of freeriding's most storied resorts.

places.name: St. Moritz
places.why: Birthplace of Alpine winter tourism, with sun-soaked, wide-open Engadin terrain above a glamorous lake town.

places.name: Davos
places.why: A high, snow-sure Graubünden town linking six separate ski areas across a broad alpine valley.

places.name: Klosters
places.why: Quieter and more traditional than neighbouring Davos, sharing the same Parsenn lift network.

places.name: Engelberg-Titlis
places.why: A rotating cable car up the glaciated Titlis gives lift-served access to steep off-piste above a monastery village.

places.name: Andermatt
places.why: Recently redeveloped and linked to Sedrun, with some of the most avalanche-prone, serious freeride terrain in Switzerland.

places.name: Saas-Fee
places.why: A glacier village ringed by 4,000-metre peaks, with lift-served snow reliable almost year-round.

places.name: Grindelwald / Jungfrau
places.why: Runs directly under the north faces of the Eiger and Jungfrau, reached by cogwheel trains instead of roads.

places.name: Crans-Montana
places.why: A sunny, south-facing balcony resort above the Rhône valley, popular for its long groomers and views.

places.name: St. Anton am Arlberg
places.why: The cradle of Alpine ski technique, now linked into the largest connected ski area in Austria.

places.name: Kitzbühel
places.why: Home to the Hahnenkamm, the most feared downhill race course in the World Cup calendar.

places.name: Sölden
places.why: Two glaciers keep this Ötztal resort snow-sure and it regularly opens the World Cup ski season in October.

places.name: Ischgl
places.why: High, snow-sure Silvretta terrain linked across the border to Samnaun, Switzerland, for duty-free shopping runs.

places.name: Zell am See-Kaprun
places.why: Lakeside town skiing linked to the Kitzsteinhorn glacier above Kaprun for near year-round snow.

places.name: Obergurgl-Hochgurgl
places.why: One of the highest villages in Austria, almost guaranteeing snow from November to May.

places.name: Mayrhofen / Hintertux Glacier
places.why: Steep terrain and the Harakiri piste, plus the Hintertux Glacier's genuine 365-day skiing further up the valley.

places.name: Saalbach-Hinterglemm
places.why: A wide, sunny bowl of interlinked villages that forms one of Austria's biggest and liveliest ski circuits.

places.name: Lech-Zürs
places.why: The quiet, exclusive end of the Arlberg, with dependable snow and some of the most understated luxury in the Alps.

places.name: Cortina d'Ampezzo
places.why: Dolomite spires ring one of skiing's most scenic resorts, host of the 1956 and upcoming 2026 Winter Olympics.

places.name: Val Gardena
places.region: Selva di Val Gardena, South Tyrol
places.why: Part of the Sella Ronda circuit, a legendary lift-and-piste loop around the Sella massif in the Dolomites.

places.name: Alta Badia
places.why: The other flank of the Sella Ronda, known for scenic groomers and mountain-hut dining right on the piste.

places.name: Sestriere
places.why: Host of the 2006 Winter Olympics and the hub of the Milky Way's cross-border Italian-French ski link.

places.name: Livigno
places.why: A duty-free valley town at 1,800 m with reliably cold, dry snow into the shoulder seasons.

places.name: Courmayeur
places.why: The Italian side of Mont Blanc, joined by cable car to Chamonix's Vallée Blanche descent.

places.name: Madonna di Campiglio
places.why: An elegant Dolomite-adjacent resort with wide groomers and some of Italy's best-known off-piste, the Canalone Miramonti.

places.name: Bormio
places.why: A World Cup downhill venue, the Stelvio, dropping over 1,000 vertical metres from a historic spa town.

places.name: Passo dello Stelvio
places.why: Summer glacier skiing on Europe's highest paved pass, a long-running training ground for racers.

places.name: Garmisch-Partenkirchen (Zugspitze)
places.why: Lift-served glacier skiing on Germany's highest peak, plus classic Kandahar downhill terrain below.

places.name: Kranjska Gora
places.why: Slovenia's biggest resort and a regular World Cup slalom venue beneath the Julian Alps.

places.name: Vogel
places.why: A cable-car-served balcony resort above Lake Bohinj inside Triglav National Park.

places.name: Baqueira-Beret
places.why: The largest and snowiest resort in the Spanish Pyrenees, long favoured by the Spanish royal family.

places.name: Sierra Nevada
places.why: Europe's southernmost major ski resort, close enough to the Mediterranean coast to ski and swim the same day.

places.name: Formigal
places.why: One of the largest resorts in the Pyrenees, with wide, sunny bowls above the Tena valley.

places.name: Grandvalira
places.why: The biggest ski area in the Pyrenees and southern Europe, spanning Andorra's eastern valleys.

places.name: Åre
places.why: Scandinavia's premier ski resort and a regular World Cup slalom stop on a lake-side mountain.

places.name: Riksgränsen
places.why: Skiing under the midnight sun into June, this far above the Arctic Circle the season ends in daylight, not darkness.

places.name: Trysil
places.why: Norway's largest ski resort, a family-oriented mountain close to the Swedish border.

places.name: Hemsedal
places.why: Norway's steepest lift-served terrain, nicknamed the Scandinavian Alps for its jagged skyline.

places.name: Narvikfjellet
places.why: Steep, fjord-side freeride terrain above the Arctic port that supplied Sweden's iron ore, with heli access nearby.

places.name: Geilo
places.why: One of Norway's oldest ski towns, with gentle terrain that has made it a family staple for a century.

places.name: Levi
places.why: Finland's best-known resort and an annual World Cup slalom opener under frequent aurora displays.

places.name: Ylläs
places.why: Finland's biggest connected ski area, spread across twin fells inside Lapland's fell country.

places.name: Bansko
places.why: Bulgaria's biggest and snowiest resort, valued across Europe for low prices and a long groomed run to town.

places.name: Borovets
places.why: Bulgaria's oldest resort, with wide, tree-lined pistes below Mount Musala.

places.name: Pamporovo
places.why: A gentle, forested resort marketed as one of the sunniest in the Balkans.

places.name: Jahorina
places.why: A 1984 Winter Olympic downhill venue rebuilt into Bosnia's most developed ski area.

places.name: Kopaonik
places.why: Serbia's largest resort, on a high, sunny plateau with the country's most reliable snow cover.

places.name: Poiana Brașov
places.why: Romania's best-known resort, a gondola ride above a medieval Transylvanian town.

places.name: Gudauri
places.why: Wide-open, largely treeless Caucasus terrain that has made Georgia a fast-rising freeride destination.

places.name: Mestia (Hatsvali/Tetnuldi)
places.why: Remote Svaneti peaks above a UNESCO-listed medieval tower village, with heli access to untouched terrain.

places.name: Rosa Khutor
places.why: The alpine venue of the 2014 Sochi Olympics, with the Caucasus's most modern lift infrastructure.

places.name: Elbrus (Cheget/Terskol)
places.why: Skiing on the flanks of Europe's highest peak, a rugged, high-altitude freeride classic.

places.name: Erciyes
places.why: Turkey's largest ski area, on the slopes of a dormant volcano above the Cappadocia region.

places.name: Palandöken
places.why: High, snow-sure eastern Anatolian terrain with some of Turkey's longest and steepest runs.

places.name: Shymbulak
places.why: Central Asia's biggest resort, a gondola ride above Almaty into the snowy Tian Shan foothills.

places.name: Mzaar Kfardebian
places.why: The largest ski area in the Middle East, close enough to Beirut for skiing and the coast in a single day.

places.name: Niseko (Grand Hirafu)
places.why: Siberian storms deliver some of the most consistent, driest powder on the planet to this Hokkaido town.

places.name: Rusutsu
places.why: Deep tree skiing across three interlinked peaks, quieter than neighbouring Niseko but just as snowy.

places.name: Kiroro
places.why: Among Hokkaido's snowiest resorts, with wide-open bowls and reliably light, dry snow.

places.name: Asahidake
places.why: A single ropeway onto Hokkaido's highest peak, opening backcountry powder terrain with no marked pistes.

places.name: Tomamu
places.why: A purpose-built Hokkaido resort known for its cloud sea viewpoint and reliable, sheltered tree runs.

places.name: Hakuba (Happo-One)
places.why: Host of the 1998 Nagano Olympics, with the biggest vertical and steepest terrain in the Japan Alps.

places.name: Nozawa Onsen
places.why: A century-old hot-spring village resort with steep upper pitches and public bathhouses at the base.

places.name: Myoko Kogen
places.why: Some of the heaviest snowfall in Japan, feeding old-school resorts on the flanks of a dormant volcano.

places.name: Shiga Kogen
places.why: Japan's largest ski area, 21 linked ski areas on one lift pass inside a national park.

places.name: Zao Onsen
places.why: Famous for its juhyo, wind-sculpted snow monsters formed on frozen fir trees along the upper runs.

places.name: Furano
places.why: A former World Cup venue in central Hokkaido, prized for dry snow with far fewer crowds than the coast.

places.name: Naeba
places.why: One of Japan's biggest single resorts, linked by gondola to Kagura for a huge combined terrain.

places.name: Appi Kogen
places.why: Long, wide groomers on volcanic Mount Iwate, developed with a resort standard rare in the Tohoku region.

places.name: Yongpyong
places.why: South Korea's oldest and largest resort, and the alpine skiing venue for the 2018 Winter Olympics.

places.name: High1 Resort
places.why: Korea's highest-altitude resort, built on a former coal-mining mountain in Gangwon Province.

places.name: Yabuli
places.why: China's oldest major ski resort and long-time national training base, in the country's coldest province.

places.name: Changbaishan (Wanda)
places.why: A purpose-built resort near the Changbai volcanic range, among China's snowiest ski destinations.

places.name: Gulmarg
places.why: Asia's highest cable car opens huge, ungroomed Himalayan bowls above a single sleepy meadow village.

places.name: Auli
places.why: A small Garhwal Himalaya resort with views of Nanda Devi, developed as India's main ski-racing venue.

places.name: Solang Valley
places.why: The most accessible ski slopes in the Indian Himalaya, a short drive above the backpacker town of Manali.

places.name: Malam Jabba
places.why: Pakistan's only developed ski resort, rebuilt in the Swat Valley after years of closure.

places.name: Naltar Valley
places.why: A remote Karakoram valley used by Pakistan's ski federation, with untouched backcountry bowls.

places.name: Treble Cone
places.why: The biggest lift-served vertical and the steepest, widest open faces in the Southern Lakes region.

places.name: Cardrona Alpine Resort
places.why: Wide, sunny beginner-to-intermediate basins that have made this one of New Zealand's most family-friendly resorts.

places.name: Coronet Peak
places.why: Queenstown's original ski field, with night skiing and views over the Wakatipu basin.

places.name: The Remarkables
places.why: Jagged, alpine terrain named for the mountain range it sits in, above Lake Wakatipu.

places.name: Mt Hutt
places.why: Canterbury's biggest ski area, exposed and often windy, but with one of the longest seasons on the South Island.

places.name: Craigieburn Valley
places.why: A rope-tow, club-run field with steep, ungroomed terrain that draws serious backcountry-minded skiers.

places.name: Mt Olympus
places.why: A classic Kiwi club field: nutcracker rope tows, no snowmaking, and steep, ungroomed Canterbury terrain.

places.name: Temple Basin
places.why: A hike-in club field reached on foot from Arthur's Pass, with rope tows and a strong DIY culture.

places.name: Whakapapa (Mt Ruapehu)
places.why: The North Island's largest ski area, on an active volcano with views across the whole central plateau.

places.name: Ohau Snow Fields
places.why: A tiny, uncrowded club-style field above Lake Ohau, run more for locals than tourists.

places.name: Perisher
places.why: Australia's largest ski resort, four linked areas across the Snowy Mountains.

places.name: Thredbo
places.why: Australia's longest runs and biggest vertical drop, in an alpine village at the foot of Mount Kosciuszko.

places.name: Falls Creek
places.why: A ski-in-ski-out Victorian alpine village with wide beginner terrain and a lively cross-country scene.

places.name: Mt Buller
places.why: The closest major resort to Melbourne, with a small alpine village atop the mountain itself.

places.name: Mt Hotham
places.why: Victoria's highest resort, known for the most reliably powdery snow on Australia's mainland.

places.name: Mt Baw Baw
places.why: A small, family-run Victorian field, the closest ski area to Melbourne by driving distance.

places.name: Ski Portillo
places.why: A yellow lakeside hotel below the Andes crest, closed to day visitors so the powder stays for guests all week.

places.name: Valle Nevado
places.why: The highest and largest of the resorts above Santiago, with heli-ski and cat-ski access beyond its lifts.

places.name: La Parva
places.why: A quieter, more local resort in the Tres Valles above Santiago, linked to El Colorado and Valle Nevado.

places.name: El Colorado / Farellones
places.why: The closest ski area to Santiago, an easy day trip up from the capital into the Andes.

places.name: Nevados de Chillán
places.why: Volcanic terrain and Chile's longest run, plus natural hot springs at the base after a day of skiing.

places.name: Corralco
places.why: A small, uncrowded resort on an active volcano in Chile's Araucanía region, known for its tree skiing.

places.name: Volcán Villarrica (Pucón)
places.why: Lift-served skiing on the flanks of one of South America's most active volcanoes, above the lakeside town of Pucón.

places.name: Antillanca
places.why: A remote volcanic-crater resort inside Puyehue National Park in Chile's Lake District.

places.name: Las Leñas
places.why: Legendary, treeless Andean bowls that made this Argentina's benchmark for extreme lift-served skiing.

places.name: Cerro Catedral
places.why: South America's biggest ski area, above a lakeside Patagonian town with Alpine-style architecture.

places.name: Chapelco
places.region: San Martín de los Andes, Neuquén
places.why: Wide, tree-lined Patagonian terrain with views over Lanín volcano and the lakes district.

places.name: Cerro Bayo
places.why: A small, sheltered resort above a lakeside village on the Patagonian Seven Lakes route.

places.name: Cerro Castor
places.why: The southernmost ski resort on earth, with a season stretching into October at the tip of Patagonia.

places.name: Oukaïmeden
places.why: Africa's highest ski resort, a single-lift outpost in the High Atlas above Marrakesh.

places.name: Afriski
places.why: Southern Africa's only real ski resort, on a high, snow-catching pass in the Maloti Mountains.

places.name: Chréa
places.why: A small, historic resort in the Atlas Mountains close enough to Algiers for a day trip to the snow.
